messages:
Elaine: Quick sync — I'm drafting the PRD for Keystore + Audit Log retention; this is customer-driven (enterprise A) and needs to meet SOC2 evidence requirements. Meeting in 30 but posting thread for async notes. Main asks: 1) configurable retention per tenant (30/90/365), 2) KMS/HSM separation for key material, 3) immutable audit exports. @Ravi can you confirm HSM constraints re: exportability? @Nora any redlines from compliance?
Ravi: Short answer: HSMs cannot export private key material unless you use wrapped keys. We can provide key references and signing ops from HSM, but not raw keys. For retention: HSM logs are separate; we can store signing events but not key blobs. :lock:
Nora: From compliance: SOC2/ISO require tamper-evident audit trails and time-of-event retention guarantees. Retention policy must include deletion proof for deletions after retention window. 30/90/365 looks fine but need policy for legal holds and export for audits.
Sam: Infra notes — storing full audit logs indefinitely is expensive. Proposal: hot storage for 90 days, cold archived snapshots for 1+ years in write-once object store (WORM) for tamper-resistance. We can integrate with customer S3 if they need private control.
Priya: Engineering constraints — to support per-tenant retention and legal holds we need per-tenant metadata, TTLs, and a retention-enforcement service. Edge case: if customer asks for immediate deletion, we must confirm no legal hold. Also need key rotation handling for past audit entries referencing rotated keys.
Jon: From solutions side: several customers request per-region retention windows and separate billing for long-term archive. Also they want a KMS/HSM audit event schema — can we agree on a minimal event model? Suggest fields: timestamp, tenant_id, op_type (sign/unwrap), key_id, result, request_id.
Maya: Customer success — flagged one customer who requires HSM-backed keys + 7-year audit retention for EU regulatory reasons. They're willing to pay for archive. Keep that in mind for prioritization.
deploy-bot: New RFC draft uploaded: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/keystore-retention-v1 — please comment by EOD.
Elaine: Draft acceptance criteria (quick):
```
- AC1: Tenant-level retention tiers (30/90/365/3650) configurable in Console and via API.
- AC2: Audit export: produce WORM snapshots with cryptographic integrity proof and ability to verify signature chain.
- AC3: Keys in HSM must never be exportable; all sign/unwrap ops routed to HSM with key_id references.
- AC4: Legal hold overrides retention deletion; audit evidence for holds retained until release.
- AC5: Documentation + SOC2 evidence pack (retention policy, export samples, key handling) available for review.
```
Please call out any missing edge cases. Prioritization thought: V1 should aim for 90-day hot + billed archive for longer. 3650 (7y) can be an enterprise add-on.
Ravi: Addendum on AC2: need to surface a signed manifest listing file checksums and a signing key (we can use HSM signing). Also clarify chain of custody for archived objects.
Nora: Add: retention policy should be configurable but defaults must meet SOC2 baseline (90 days). Also require a periodic integrity check job report for auditors.
Priya: Implementation note: we'll need a retention-enforcer + archive-worker + API flags. Estimate: 3 sprints for minimal 90-day + export, +2 sprints for per-tenant custom tiers and legal-hold UI.
Jon: For prioritization: mark export + signed manifest as P0 for any enterprise sale. Per-tenant UI can be P1.
Elaine: Great. Action items:
- Priya: put architecture spike + rough timeline by EOD Thu
- Ravi & Nora: add compliance checklist items into RFC (encryption-at-rest, HSM constraints, manifest schema)
- Jon & Maya: surface customer commitments and willingness-to-pay
- I'll fold this into PRD and send for review.
Elaine: Thanks everyone — if no objections I'll mark RFC reviewer deadline for Friday noon. :thumbsup:
